headline: Committee sends vehicle noise fine bill to full council

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: The committee voted to send Bill 119-2025, which would raise fines for loud vehicle sound systems, to the full council.
meeting.recap: The committee had one item: Bill 119-2025, about penalties for prohibited noise violations.[[0:03:48]] One person testified that the fines seemed too high for poor people.[[0:09:52]] The bill would raise fines for loud vehicle sound systems and allow the systems to be taken away, called forfeiture.[[0:11:03]] The committee chair prepared a revised version, called CD1, that removes forfeiture from the third offense and raises fines for first and second offenses.[[0:12:03]] The chair said state law does not allow fines for these violations to go above $1,000.[[0:12:20]] A deputy prosecuting attorney said the department supports the revised version without forfeiture.[[0:15:33]] The deputy prosecuting attorney said unpaid fines block people from renewing their driver's license.[[0:15:40]] Chair Lee, who introduced the bill, said loud music is a problem in Wailuku and asked members to pass it.[[0:17:12]] The deputy prosecuting attorney said he has not seen anyone fight a noise ticket in court in 15 years.[[0:36:42]] The committee voted five ayes, with four members excused, to discharge Bill 119-2025.[[0:48:03]]
meeting.next: Chair Lee said the discharge moves the bill to the full council. A police sergeant said he could look into how many noise citations were given in the last year.

moments.q: "If I can save another life, if we can save another life"
